summary:
Count +1 for every 1 and −1 for every 0. A stretch has equal numbers exactly when its sum is 0, i.e. when
the running balance is the **same** at both of its ends. So for each position, the longest even stretch
ending there starts right after the **first** position with the same balance. Remember first positions
and the whole thing is one O(n) pass.

question.md:
Find the longest run of consecutive bits containing as many 0s as 1s. Return its length, or 0.

- **Consecutive:** you can't skip elements.
- **Equal counts** means the length is always even.
- **No such run** (e.g. `[1, 1, 1]`) gives 0.
- **Size:** up to 10⁵ bits, so checking all ~5 × 10⁹ runs is too slow.

think.md: Take `bits = [1, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 0, 1, 0]`. Replace each 0 with −1 and keep a running sum (the **balance**):

think.caption: A stretch is even exactly when the balance before it equals the balance at its end.

think.md:
A run from index a to index b has equal counts exactly when its +1s and −1s cancel, i.e. when
`balance after b == balance before a`. So the question becomes: **for each position, where is the earliest
position with the same balance?** The farther back that is, the longer the stretch.

The balance before any bit is 0 (think of it as position −1). Storing the first position of each balance
value as you go answers each lookup in O(1), and since the balance stays within −n … n, a plain array of
size 2n + 1 can hold the first positions. The longest here is 8.

approaches.title: Extend from every start

idea.md: For each start i, extend j to the right keeping `ones − zeros`; whenever it's 0, the stretch i … j is even, so update the best length.

build: For each j ≥ i: add +1 or −1; if balance is 0, `best = max(best, j − i + 1)`.

lines.text: Every possible starting position, with an empty balance.
Grow the stretch one bit at a time: +1 for a 1, −1 for a 0.
Balance 0 means equal counts; keep the longest.

steps.text: Start 0, end 1: ones and zeros match. New best length 2.
Start 0, end 3: ones and zeros match. New best length 4.
Start 1, end 6: ones and zeros match. New best length 6.
Start 1, end 8: ones and zeros match. New best length 8.

walk.title: Try every start; extend to every end, tracking (#1s − #0s). A balance of 0 means equal counts.

limits.md: Each start re-walks the same bits. The balance of a stretch is the difference of two running balances, so one pass plus a lookup of earlier balances is enough.

approaches.title: First position of each running balance

idea.md:
Walk once with `balance` (+1 per 1, −1 per 0). Keep `first[b]`, the earliest position where the balance
was b, with `first[0] = −1`. At position i:

- if `balance` was seen before, the stretch `first[balance] + 1 … i` is even: length `i − first[balance]`;
- otherwise record `first[balance] = i`.

Only the **first** occurrence is stored, because the earliest start gives the longest stretch. The
balance stays in −n … n, so an array with an offset of n works as the map.

build: Make `first` of size 2n + 1 filled with "unseen"; set `first[0 + n] = −1`.
Seen before: update `best` with `i − first[balance + n]`. New: store `i`.

lines.text: Earliest position of each balance value. Balance 0 is "seen" at position −1, before the first bit.

notes.java: The balance ranges over −n … n, so `balance + n` indexes an array of 2n + 1 slots; −2 marks "never seen".
notes.cpp: The balance ranges over −n … n, so `balance + n` indexes an array of 2n + 1 slots; −2 marks "never seen".
notes.c: The balance ranges over −n … n, so `balance + n` indexes an array of 2n + 1 slots; −2 marks "never seen".

lines.text: Running balance: +1 for a 1, −1 for a 0.
Same balance as at an earlier position: everything after that position up to here is even. Measuring from the first occurrence gives the longest such stretch ending here.
First time at this balance: remember where. Later positions never overwrite it, because later starts only give shorter stretches.

complexity.md: **Time O(n).** **Space O(n)** for the first positions.

steps.text: Before the first bit the balance is 0, 'seen at position −1'.
Index 0: balance 1 is new; remember position 0.
Index 1: balance 0 was first seen at -1, so positions 0…1 are even (length 2) — new best.
Index 2: balance -1 is new; remember position 2.
Index 3: balance 0 was first seen at -1, so positions 0…3 are even (length 4) — new best.
Index 4: balance 1 was first seen at 0, so positions 1…4 are even (length 4).
Index 5: balance 2 is new; remember position 5.
Index 6: balance 1 was first seen at 0, so positions 1…6 are even (length 6) — new best.
Index 7: balance 2 was first seen at 5, so positions 6…7 are even (length 2).
Index 8: balance 1 was first seen at 0, so positions 1…8 are even (length 8) — new best.

walk.title: Running balance (+1 for a 1, −1 for a 0). Two positions with the same balance enclose an even stretch. Remember the first position of each balance.

takeaways.md:
- "Equal numbers of two kinds" → map them to +1/−1; equal counts = **sum 0**.
- Subarray sum 0 ⇔ the running prefix sum repeats. For the **longest**, store each prefix value's
  **first** position.
- A prefix value with a small known range can index an array (with an offset) instead of a hash map.
